title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Scheduling Operations Agent optimises multiple resources at once
notes: claim 85: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the booking-status automation cell describes a column rather than giving an executable operation, and Microsoft documents automation for team role assignment that the briefing says is absent. Published environment credit controls also answer part of its open spending question, and Learn allows technicians to interact with goals rather than only receive schedules.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The agent requires administrator setup and enablement before dispatchers can use it; unenabled tenants do not receive usable agent capabilities.
claims.quote: Before dispatchers can use the agent, an administrator must set it up in your environment. ... Go to the Agents tab and turn on Scheduling Operations Agent (Preview).

claims.claim: No separate switch is documented for the multi-resource, goal, scope and plan capabilities.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduling Operations Agent multiple resources custom goals scopes separate enable switch. Opened soa-setup, soa-overview, soa-goals, soa-scopes and soa-plans; these describe the common agent toggle and no separate capability switch.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A batch scope determines the resources, unfulfilled requirements and existing bookings the agent considers.
claims.quote: A scope defines the set of data that a batch optimization operates over - which resources to optimize, which unfulfilled requirements to consider, and which existing bookings the agent can change.

claims.claim: Scopes store fetchXML queries rather than references to the original views.
claims.quote: A scope stores the fetchXML query that's evaluated when the optimization runs, not a reference to the view used.

claims.claim: The agent truncates scope query results that exceed optimisation limits.
claims.quote: If a query returns more records than the optimization supports, the agent truncates the list.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls

claims.quote: The agent runs as an application user that belongs to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.

claims.claim: The agent's default access permits reading and writing standard scheduling tables.
claims.quote: By default, the agent's application user can read and write the standard scheduling tables.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Assigning matching team roles grants the agent access to custom tables used by optimisations.
claims.quote: If your optimizations use custom tables, Field Service or Project Operations tables, or queries that reference other tables, assign the matching security roles to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team so that the agent can read and update those tables.

claims.claim: Changes use combined caller and application-user permissions, requiring both to have record access.
claims.quote: Each change the agent makes uses the combined permissions of the user who runs the optimization and the agent's application user, so both must have access to the affected records.

claims.claim: Users additionally need scheduling-table access, for example through Field Service - Dispatcher.
claims.quote: Each user also needs a role that grants access to the underlying scheduling tables, such as bookable resources, bookings, and resource requirements - for example, a dispatcher role like Field Service - Dispatcher.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The team must be included in field security profiles covering columns referenced by scopes or queries.

claims.claim: Without that profile access the agent might ignore column filter conditions and return incorrect results.
claims.quote: Otherwise, the agent might ignore filter conditions on those columns and return incorrect results.

claims.claim: Booking-status optimisation is configured in Field Service > Resources > Booking Settings > Booking Statuses > booking status > Optimization Method.
claims.quote: Open the Field Service app and go to the Resources area. ... Select Booking Settings > Booking Statuses. ... For each booking status, set the Optimization Method property

claims.claim: 'Set the msdyn_optimizationmethod column on the BookingStatus table' is the automation call for the control.
claims.quote: Searched: the cited BookingStatus extension and its linked base BookingStatus reference for the setting and update operation. The column exists, but the printed instruction is not an operation; the base reference documents PATCH /bookingstatuses(bookingstatusid).
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api.kind to 'rest', call to 'PATCH /bookingstatuses(bookingstatusid)', and docs to 'https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/developer/reference/entities/bookingstatus'. Replace the row note's second sentence with 'The request body sets msdyn_optimizationmethod: 192350000 (Optimize), 192350001 (Do Not Move), or 192350002 (Ignore).' Retain the existing Field Service BookingStatus source for that writable column and add the base reference to sources.

claims.claim: The cited Field Service BookingStatus extension lists the writable column without printing an HTTP operation.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service Booking Status (BookingStatus) table extends the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Booking Status (BookingStatus) table. ... Writable columns/attributes ... msdyn_OptimizationMethod
claims.fix: Remove the repeated explanation that no HTTP operation is printed as the reason for using a column description instead of a call. Replace the Governance controls sentence with 'The booking status update operation is documented in the base BookingStatus reference; the Field Service extension documents its writable msdyn_optimizationmethod column.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/developer/reference/entities/bookingstatus.

claims.claim: Apply method is reached in Resource Scheduling > Settings > Optimization > Scheduling Plans > plan > Apply method.
claims.quote: In the Settings area of the Resource Scheduling app, under Optimization, select Scheduling Plans ... For Apply method, select Review before apply or Apply automatically. ... To run the plan on demand, open it

claims.claim: PATCH /msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplans(msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplanid) updates the plan's msdyn_applymethod.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplans(msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplanid) ... Writable columns/attributes ... msdyn_Applymethod ... LogicalName | msdyn_applymethod ... 859530000 | Review before apply ... 859530001 | Apply automatically

claims.claim: Team access is assigned separately per environment through Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Teams > Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, select your environment, and then go to Settings > Teams. ... Select the Scheduling Operations Agent Team. ... Assign the security roles that grant access to the tables your optimizations use

claims.where: Governance controls: parenthesis explaining the missing team row
claims.claim: Learn documents no automation for assigning security roles to the agent's team.
claims.quote: The Associate method assigns the role to a team.
claims.fix: Remove 'it is not a row because Learn documents no automation for it' from the parenthesis. Microsoft documents programmatic team role assignment; no new control row is required by this correction.

claims.where: Open questions: credit controls beyond usage and budgets
claims.claim: Documentation of credit controls beyond viewing usage and Azure budgets remains open for limiting this agent's environment consumption.
claims.quote: Environment capacity controls apply to all Copilot Studio workloads in the environment ... Allocate a defined amount of prepaid capacity, turn off Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, and don't connect the environment to pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.fix: Remove the final Open questions bullet. Microsoft already documents environment allocation and overage controls for all Copilot Studio workloads; the setup page explicitly places this agent on those prepaid or pay-as-you-go environment billing models.

claims.claim: Technicians see only the schedules the agent produces.
claims.quote: Dispatchers and technicians can view goals and select one when they run an optimization.
claims.fix: Remove '; technicians see only the schedules the agent produces' from the impact rationale. Keep 'Medium. Dispatchers and the admins who build goals, scopes and plans notice it.' and the existing sentence about tenants that have not enabled the agent.

claims.where: Governance guidance: billing, team access, field security, credit usage and recurrence checklist items
claims.claim: Every control that the governance checklist asks readers to set or inspect appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Confirm a billing model is in place ... add it to field security profiles ... Review credit consumption ... Audit recurring plans for their Apply method and recurrence interval. Table: enablement, user roles, booking status, Apply method only.
claims.fix: The checklist's billing setup, team security roles, field security profiles, credit-consumption review, recurrence interval, and location/map prerequisites have no corresponding control rows. Record these as table-coverage gaps; do not add rows as part of this correction.
